data.narrative:
Kairos Power is a late-stage nuclear energy company founded by Mike Laufer, Edward Blandford, and Per Peterson. The company has raised over $500M to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises 10 known comparable companies: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, as the peer-median approach is not applicable. The nuclear energy sector lacks sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum density thresholds (fewer than three datapoints in narrow peer filters). The stage-progression method applies a 1.2x multiplier to the $500M total capital raised proxy, reflecting typical Late Stage advancement dynamics, yielding an implied value of $600M.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $510M to $690M, with a median of $600M. This range reflects conservative ($510M) to optimistic ($690M) scenarios within late-stage progression parameters. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage nuclear comparables to benchmark against peer multiples, the nascent maturity of the fusion and advanced fission markets, and technology-specific development risk. Any future valuation update should prioritize gathering additional late-stage nuclear private company data to enable peer-median triangulation.
